subject: Cross-cloud listing playbook: SKU split, regional packaging & co-sell asks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Azure Marketplace PM <azurepm@microsoft.com>, AWS Marketplace BD <aws-bd@amazon.com>, GCP Partner Eng <partner-eng@google.com>
Cc: CloudChannel TPX <tpx@cloudchannel.co>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-cloud listing playbook: SKU split, regional packaging & co-sell asks

Team and partners —

Following our product/BD sync last week, I put a first-pass playbook together for how we propose to list Redwood on each cloud marketplace, and where to prioritize co-sell asks vs. self-serve listings. High level asks below; attached is a draft SKU matrix and a proposed canary regional schedule. Please review and flag any infeasible asks from the marketplace side.

Key proposals (summary):
- AWS: single-metered SKU (per-token consumption) for Hosted API + Dedicated reservation SKU as separate listing; prioritize AP-NorthAmerica (us-east/us-west) for co-sell (AWS GTM team recommended).
- Azure: two SKUs — a "Starter" metered offering (self-serve) and an "Enterprise Reserved" SKU (subscription/commit) to capture dedicated customers; co-sell motion to include Azure Migration credits.
- GCP: focus on a packaged "Private + Support" SKU for customers wanting VPC/on-prem proxies; keep metered Hosted API listing but deprioritize aggressive co-sell until we validate latency SLAs.

Open questions for partners:
1) Co-sell referral cadence and contact hygiene — are there specific field contacts we should route enterprise leads to for each cloud?
2) Marketplace contract terms — any constraints around trial credits + commit discounts that would block our proposed SKU separation?
3) Can the marketplaces support our canary region gating (attach schedule) for staged rollouts per SKU?

Next steps I propose: internal review by Tue 6/29, then a short partner sync w/ marketplace PMs on Thu 7/1 to align on blockers.

Attachments: 2027-06-25_sku-matrix-draft.xlsx, canary-region-schedule.pdf

Thanks,

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Azure Marketplace PM <azurepm@microsoft.com>, AWS Marketplace BD <aws-bd@amazon.com>, GCP Partner Eng <partner-eng@google.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud listing playbook: SKU split, regional packaging & co-sell asks

Soojin — good start. Two quick product notes from my side before partner sync:

- SKU granularity: If we separate Hosted API (metered) and Dedicated (reservation) at listing time, we need clear mapping in our backend to ensure billing metering is toggleable at account-level (so we don't need a separate imaging pipeline per SKU). Ops can do this but requires a week of integration testing.
- Canary latency SLAs: GCP's private path tests showed 12–18ms tail p99 in us-central with our current edge config; that's borderline for enterprise SLAs. If GCP co-sell requires SLA guarantees for dedicated deployments, we should either push GCP to a second-phase co-sell or provision dedicated infra in a nearby region.

I'll attach a short ops checklist to the drive folder.

Jonas
Director, Product — Serving Runtime

From: Azure Marketplace PM <azurepm@microsoft.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudChannel TPX <tpx@cloudchannel.co>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud listing playbook: SKU split, regional packaging & co-sell asks

Hi Soojin / team —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. A few responses from Azure listing side: we can support a two-SKU approach (metered + reserved commitment) but need clarity on these items before we can proceed to co-sell enablement:

- Pricing floor: For reserved SKUs, Azure requires an upfront commit term (monthly/annual) and a minimum discount band. We'll need your target margin ranges to start commercial modeling.
- Trial/Free credits: Azure imposes constraints on stacking marketplace trial credits with vendor credits. If you want to offer both, we need a small legal carve-out and it can slow certification.
- Co-sell handoff: We can route enterprise leads to the Azure field team if you provide account mapping rules (e.g., ARR threshold, industry vertical). Recommend the handoff trigger be leads > $100k ARR or proof-of-concept request > 6 weeks.

On canary regional rollout: we can gate co-sell-enabled SKUs to specific Azure regions (we call them "lead regions") during initial 8-week pilots. Our field recommends US East and EU West for initial canaries.

If you can share target pricing and the final SKU matrix by EOD Mon 7/5, we can put the SKU request into our listing pipeline for a July certification window.

— Priya (Azure PM)
Priya Natarajan | Azure Marketplace Partner Management
azurepm@microsoft.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Azure Marketplace PM <azurepm@microsoft.com>, AWS Marketplace BD <aws-bd@amazon.com>, GCP Partner Eng <partner-eng@google.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudChannel TPX <tpx@cloudchannel.co>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud listing playbook: SKU split, regional packaging & co-sell asks

Thanks Priya — good clarity. Quick commitments from our side to unblock certification: 

1) Pricing and margin bands: product will deliver a target price sheet by EOD Tue 7/6. We will propose a reserved-commit discount band of 20–30% with minimum 12-month commitment for enterprise SKU.
2) Handoff rules: we accept the ARR > $100k / POC > 6 weeks trigger for co-sell. We will include account mapping in the playbook and add a routing table for Azure field contacts.
3) Canary regions: we will align our canary schedule to start with US East and EU West for Azure; AWS will use us-east-1 and eu-west-1; GCP we will hold canary until latency validation is complete (tentative start: 2027-08-01).

Action items assigned:
- Jonas: finalize infra gating checklist and update Drive (due 7/6).
- Karthik: finalize SKU names + metering attributes for each cloud and upload price sheet (due 7/6).
- Ben: confirm co-sell routing and GTM contacts for AWS and GCP (due 7/6).

If partners are comfortable with the timeline, we'll open formal listing requests on 7/7.

Best,

Soojin
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
